# Implementation Accelerator Proposal

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Implementation Accelerator, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has three AI use cases at different stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. The EU AI Act and GDPR are the stated regulatory drivers.

Three constraints shape the work:

- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.
- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

The stated objective, in Dana Whitfield's words, is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

## 2. Why an Intensive AIMS Foundation Build Fits Now

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. The stated production target for visual inspection is Q2 2027. ISO/IEC 42001 work is planned to start next year, with no fixed start date.

Together these points favor building the foundation of an Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) early and in a concentrated form. Doing so gives the Client the following:

- **A direct response to the audit finding.** The missing AI system inventory is built and classified during the week.
- **Time for adoption before Q2 2027.** Drafted governance artifacts can move through review and adoption by the Client's own governance bodies before the stated production target. Adoption timing remains a Client decision.
- **ISO/IEC 42001 readiness without front-loaded cost.** Artifacts are structured for future conformity work under ISO/IEC 42001. The Accelerator builds readiness. It does not deliver or promise certification.
- **Integration with existing systems.** Building on the ISMS and quality management system avoids a parallel governance structure that the Client would later need to reconcile.

The week is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. In practice this means the Client's people make every classification and risk decision and own every artifact at close.

## 3. Five-Day Build Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

Dependencies are sequenced deliberately. The charter precedes the policies, and the inventory precedes the risk register.

| Day | Build focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Governance charter and roles | Define decision rights across legal, security, quality, data and plant operations. Record the works council consultation requirement as a governance step. Identify ISMS and quality management system attachment points, where they exist (currently `Unknown`). |
| 2 | AI system inventory and classification | Enter the chatbot, the visual inspection pilot and the planned sales forecasting use case as first entries. Apply a classification scheme with EU AI Act orientation fields. |
| 3 | Risk and impact assessment plus risk register | Assess each inventoried system. Seed risk statements as drafts for Client validation. Structure the register to attach to existing risk processes, where they exist (currently `Unknown`). |
| 4 | Core policies and operating procedures | Draft acceptable use, lifecycle governance, vendor and supplier governance, incident response and change management. Carry the EU data residency constraint into the vendor and data provisions. |
| 5 | Evidence model, implementation priorities and executive readout | Map artifacts to assurance questions. Prioritize next steps against the stated Q2 2027 production target. Present to the executive checkpoint. |

**Attachment points.** The Client's ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 systems are the intended attachment points for every artifact. The specific registers, procedures or records each artifact will attach to are `Unknown` at this stage. Framework certification or adoption is not evidence that any particular register, process, control or record exists. These attachment points will be confirmed with the build team on Day 1.

**Regulatory mapping.** Mapping to the EU AI Act and GDPR is provided as orientation only. Any classification of a system under the EU AI Act, and any item with legal effect, carries the note: confirm with external counsel.

**Works council.** No artifact touching production staff will be presented as ready for adoption until the works council consultation the Client has stated as required has taken place. The current status of that consultation is `Unknown`.

## 4. Artifacts the Client Owns at Close

Each artifact leaves the week with a status of draft or reviewed. Adoption follows through the Client's own governance.

1. AI governance charter: purpose, scope, roles, decision rights and meeting cadence.
2. Roles and decision rights matrix.
3. AI system inventory, with the chatbot, the visual inspection pilot and the planned sales forecasting use case as first entries.
4. AI system classification scheme, with EU AI Act orientation fields (confirm with external counsel).
5. AI risk and impact assessment method.
6. AI risk register, with seeded risk statements labeled as drafts for Client validation.
7. Acceptable use policy (draft).
8. AI lifecycle governance policy (draft).
9. Vendor and supplier governance policy (draft), including the stated EU customer data constraint.
10. AI incident response procedure (draft).
11. AI change management procedure (draft).
12. Framework attachment map to the ISMS and quality management system, with unconfirmed points rendered `Unknown`.
13. Evidence model and evidence index, mapping each artifact to the assurance question it answers and structured for ISO/IEC 42001 readiness.
14. Prioritized implementation plan.
15. Executive readout pack.

## 5. Frameworks Used

- **GRC Workbook** (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) provides the structure for the inventory, the risk register and the evidence model.
- **Slow AI Kitchen** (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) provides the working method for deliberate, human-led decisions during build sessions.
- **AI Governance for Boards** (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) serves as the board-layer reference for the Day 5 executive readout.

## 6. Team Composition Asked of the Client

We ask the Client to designate a build team covering these roles for all five days:

- General Counsel
- CISO
- Head of Quality
- Head of Data
- German plant manager
- Two internal auditors

We suggest the Client decide in advance how the two internal auditors take part so that internal audit independence is preserved for future assurance work. For example, they could act in a challenge and review capacity rather than as artifact owners.

Executive checkpoint attendance is required on Days 1 and 5. The executive attendees are `Unknown` and are to be named by the Client.

## 7. Logistics and Price

- **Format:** five consecutive working days of live virtual working sessions, with structured build time each day.
- **Dates:** `Unknown`, to be scheduled with the Client.
- **Price:** US$25,000. This sits within the stated approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a short scheduling call to:

- confirm the Accelerator dates;
- confirm the named build team and executive checkpoint attendees;
- confirm the status of the works council consultation;
- collect the existing ISMS and quality management system documents needed for Day 1.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
